ConocoPhillips rose 1.64% today, closing at $132.49, as oil markets gained ground on geopolitical tensions—specifically fresh U.S. strikes on Iranian targets that pushed Brent crude above $90 per barrel. The stock had dipped significantly over the prior week but recovered on the back of this energy price lift. As a major oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude prices rise, since higher oil commands higher revenues.

The broader context matters too: while Trump's announcement of control over Venezuela's oil reserves and his push to boost U.S. refining capacity could theoretically add long-term supply pressure, the immediate market reaction has favored energy prices, likely because geopolitical risk (Iran tensions, Russia's threatened strikes on Ukrainian energy sites) is keeping oil in higher demand right now.
